newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-M.A. Hanna looks to overseas buys.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-M.A. Hanna looks to overseas buys.

text.p: M.A. Hanna aims to grow its overseas business from around 21 percent of sales to 25 percent by 2001 and is actively looking at acquisitions in Europe to achieve that.

Doug McGregor, who on Wednesday was elected chairman of the Cleveland, Ohio-based specialty chemicals company told Reuters in a telephone interview that Hanna could achieve 8-10 percent annual growth in earnings internally, but had to look outside to achieve a total of 15 percent.
"We are looking at one or two reasonably good-sized acquisitions, which will add $75-$100 million of revenues, primarily in Europe," McGregor said.
M.A. Hanna last September said it aimed to increase sales to $4.0 billion by 2001 from $2.1 billion in 1996 and that would mean international sales rising to $1.0 billion.

Last year, the acquisition of three companies led to 13 percent growth in manufacturing sales. The company, which makes plastics and rubber compounds and distributes engineered plastic shapes, would be happy to raise debt from 31 percent of equity to fund an attractive acquisition, he said.
The company, like many other U.S. businesses is aiming to expand in the rapidly developing economies of Asia, is also looking at joint ventures in the region.

"What makes us different from other businesses is that we have had a presence there through distribution for some time," McGregor said. Hanna picked up two or three major wins in the automotive business from rivals for its resins and in the appliance industry. The distribution business, although less profitable than manufacturing, was generating good cashflow and total returns there were high because it did not have intensive capital requirements.

Asked if he thought the stock was fairly valued, McGregor noted total returns for shareholders was 22 percent a year. This year, the stock outperformed its peer group, losing four percent of its value compared with seven for the sector.
M.A. Hanna closed at 21-5/8 on Wednesday.
McGregor said the company was actively looking at share repurchases and bought back 375,000 shares in the first quarter of this year.
"We bought back 1.4 million shares in 1996 and we are probably looking at a similar number this year," he said.
Hanna was comfortable with analysts' forecasts of $1.44 in earnings per share for 1997 after $1.26 in 1996.
"There are provisos. The economy has to keep growing at two-and-a-half to three percent a year. If it does, we can keep growing at three times that level," McGregor said.
